Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC pattern note: binary mask intersection

Observed one ARC task with a vertical composite row layout: each row contained a left binary pattern, a one-cell separator column, and a right binary mask of matching width. The left pattern used 0 and 3; separator was 1; the right mask used 0 and 3. Rule inferred and verified: retain the left-pattern 3 only where the corresponding right-mask cell is also 3, and render the retained cells as 2; all other output cells are 0. Output has the shared panel dimensions (separator and mask are not included).

Demo variant used a horizontal separator: top binary image, separator row of 4s, then a mostly-1 mask with one 0. Output preserved top-image 1s only where mask was 1, recolored to 2; zeros remained 0. General rule: elementwise AND/intersection of the two binary panels, then encode foreground as 2 and background as 0. Determine orientation and separator from the grid; panels are corresponding same-sized regions.

## Aligned equal-color marker spans (task-54e2b1e9)
For each row and column, connect occurrences of the same non-background marker color: recolor cells strictly between the extreme aligned endpoints to 3, preserving the original endpoints and other cells. Find endpoints from original input; combine horizontal and vertical fills. Verified on three demos and a correct test submission. Not a flood-fill or background-wide transformation. See continual_arc_task-54e2b1e9.md.
